schedules.timeZoneNote: Runs are shown in the cron time zone, {{zone}}.

cron.label: Cron expression
cron.help: Second minute hour day month weekday (year optional). Aliases such as @daily work too
cron.empty: Enter an expression to see what it means and when it runs.
cron.secondsAdded: This expression has five fields; it is saved as "{{expression}}", with a zero seconds field first.
cron.bothDays: Both the day of the month and the day of the week are given: conductor runs only on days matching both (AND), unlike the usual cron, which runs on days matching either.
cron.noRun: No run time found for this expression: {{detail}}
cron.timeZoneUnset: No cron time zone is configured, so runs are computed in UTC; this may differ from conductor's (CONDUCTOR_CRON_TIMEZONE).
cron.daylightSaving: {{zone}} observes daylight saving time. conductor keeps using the UTC offset from when it registered the schedule, so after a change actual runs may differ from the times shown.
cron.unavailable: conductor's cron rules could not be loaded, so expressions cannot be checked. Saving is not possible until they load.
cron.timeZoneRejected: conductor cannot read the time zone "{{name}}", so it runs schedules in UTC; the runs are computed in UTC too.

export.title: Export
export.description: Download every setting (servers, schedules, Slack events, result handlers) as one TOML file, with descriptions and enabled state.
export.enabledHelp: The servers the exported settings run on are included even when disabled, so the file can be imported as it is.
export.managedNotice: These settings keep their workflow definition in a jobworkerp worker, and the TOML file only names that worker. Back the workers up separately, e.g. from admin-ui.
export.leftOut_one: {{count}} setting was left out of the file: the server it runs on has been deleted
export.leftOut_other: {{count}} settings were left out of the file: the servers they run on have been deleted

import.title: Import
import.description: Validate a TOML file first, then import it. Nothing is written unless every entry can be imported.
import.tomlHelp: Choose a file, drop one here, or paste the content.
import.overwriteHelp: Overwriting deletes every existing setting first, then imports the file. Execution history is kept.
import.newIds: Imported settings get new IDs, so execution history recorded before no longer links to them.
import.reuseServers: A server with the same name and address as an existing one is reused; any other name already in use is an error.
import.changed: The content or the overwrite option changed; validate again.
import.invalid_one: {{count}} entry cannot be imported; nothing will be written:
import.invalid_other: {{count}} entries cannot be imported; nothing will be written:
